name: Crucible Industries Resonance Katana RK-7 'Singing Edge'
description:
A katana-profile blade constructed from layered carbon-lattice composite with an integrated piezoelectric vibration system that oscillates the cutting edge at 40,000 cycles per second. The RK-7's blade appears to shimmer slightly when activated — a visual artifact of the micro-vibration that gives the weapon its name. The harmonic frequency was specifically chosen to match the resonant failure point of common body armor polymers, allowing the blade to slice through protective materials that would stop a conventional edge.

Crucible Industries developed the Resonance Katana as a prestige product for their executive protection line — a melee weapon elegant enough to be carried openly in corporate settings without appearing crude, while maintaining genuine combat lethality. The handle houses a micro-capacitor that powers the vibration system for approximately four hours of continuous use, and the blade's carbon-lattice construction makes it lighter than a traditional steel katana while being substantially harder.

The weapon has found an unexpected secondary market among GLMZ's dueling culture, where augmented combatants settle disputes in semi-legal arenas. The Singing Edge's ability to defeat armor while remaining a recognizably traditional weapon form has made it the prestige choice for duelists who value aesthetics alongside function. Master bladesmiths at Crucible hand-tune each blade's resonance frequency, and no two Singing Edges produce exactly the same tone.
legality: Licensed — registered melee weapon, executive carry permit

blade_length: 71 cm
total_length: 102 cm
weight: 0.9 kg
edge_oscillation: 40,000 Hz
power_source: Handle-integrated micro-capacitor, 4 hours continuous
blade_material: Layered carbon-lattice composite
hardness: 78 HRC equivalent
tactical_use: The Singing Edge is deployed in close-quarters situations where firearms are impractical, prohibited, or undesirable. Executive bodyguards carry it as a secondary weapon for scenarios where gunfire would cause unacceptable collateral damage. In dueling contexts, the blade's vibration system allows it to defeat opponents' armor without requiring superhuman striking force, leveling the field between augmented and unaugmented combatants. Operators learn to use the audible hum as a psychological weapon — the sound of a Singing Edge activating has ended more confrontations than the blade itself.
cultural_context: The katana form carries cultural weight in GLMZ that transcends its Japanese origins — after generations of diaspora mixing, the weapon represents discipline and martial tradition without belonging exclusively to any heritage. Crucible's decision to build a high-tech katana was a calculated cultural play, and it worked. Owning a Singing Edge signals both wealth and martial competence. The dueling community has developed a ranking system based partly on the tonal quality of a duelist's blade — higher-pitched resonance is considered more prestigious.
story_hooks: A Singing Edge was used in a high-profile duel and the blade's resonance frequency matched a tone that caused a spectator's cochlear implant to malfunction — raising questions about whether the weapon was deliberately tuned to harm augmented bystanders.

A Crucible master bladesmith has gone independent and is producing unauthorized Singing Edges with custom resonance tuning that can defeat specific armor types on request. Crucible wants them shut down.
related_entities: SynapTech Resonance Direct Neural-to-Medium Creative Interfa

physical_description.visual_profile: A katana-profile blade with an elegant, almost liquid shimmer along its cutting edge when activated. The silhouette is traditionally Japanese — slightly curved, balanced, dignified — but the subtle iridescence and barely-visible vibration distortion mark it as cutting-edge military hardware. At rest, it appears almost serene; activated, it seems to exist in a state of controlled violence.
physical_description.dimensions: Blade length: 71 cm; Total length: 102 cm; Blade width at base: approximately 3.2 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Exceptionally light and balanced — only 0.9 kg total — creating a sensation of responsive grace in the hand rather than heft. The weight distribution favors the blade slightly, encouraging fluid cutting motions without requiring muscular compensation.
physical_description.primary_material: Layered carbon-lattice composite blade with aerospace-grade polymer and brushed titanium alloy in the handle and tsuba
physical_description.finish: The blade exhibits a subtle satin-gray finish with an opalescent sheen along the edge that intensifies when the piezoelectric system activates. The handle features a matte charcoal polymer with brushed titanium accents. The tsuba is polished titanium with geometric etchings.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: gun-metal gray blade with pearl-white opalescent edge shimmer (when active). Handle: charcoal matte with titanium silver accents. Accent: subtle blue micro-LED indicators along the handle base (power/frequency status).
physical_description.grip_texture: Tightly wrapped in black synthetic cord with raised diamond-pattern grip points, providing secure purchase even with synth-skin gloves or augmented hands. The handle tapers naturally toward the pommel.
distinctive_features: Shimmer/iridescence along the cutting edge intensifying during vibration activation
Subtly visible harmonic distortion around the blade's edge (like heat shimmer) when powered
Embedded blue micro-LED status indicators (three small dots) along the handle base showing power level and resonance tuning
Precision etchings on the tsuba depicting a sound-wave pattern
Exposed micro-capacitor housing at the handle base with visible cooling vents
The blade produces an audible 40 kHz harmonic hum when activated — visible in the air as a faint shimmer
Hand-tuned frequency calibration plate etched into the blade near the tang (unique serial tuning data per unit)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CRUCIBLE INDUSTRIES logo embossed in the tsuba center. Model designation 'RK-7' engraved along the upper handle in minimalist sans-serif lettering. Hand-tuning certificate hologram embedded beneath the grip wrapping, visible from the side. Serial number etched into the blade tang.
physical_description.condition_typical: When freshly maintained: pristine, gleaming, barely-visible wear. In active duelist hands: minimal wear (blade doesn't dull from vibration), possible shallow scratches on the flat from blocked strikes, grip wrapping occasionally re-tied. Corporate executive carry: museum-condition, regularly inspected. Street duelists' blades: battle-worn polymer handle, micro-scratches on the blade surface, faint discoloration from sweat/blood, grip rewrapped with personal touches.
